headline: I design and deliver cloud platforms and integrations — on Azure, with Terraform — and connect AI assistants to them, safely.
lede: Organisations hire me when a platform has to be designed, wired to the systems around it, and actually run in production: infrastructure as code, APIs and message flows, and the connectors that let AI assistants use all of it — within your security rules.
examples_title: What it looks like in practice
ex1_body: transaction orchestration, business-rule checks, SWIFT messaging, data models and migrations — from design to user acceptance testing.
ex2_body: Terraform-managed Azure environments: Front Door and WAF, private networking, virtual desktops, reproducible dev, test and production.
ex3_title: Plugging the intranet into Claude and ChatGPT
ex3_body: MCP connectors that let employees search, read and publish intranet content from their AI assistant, within their own permissions.
ex4_body: AI coding agents running in sandboxes (containers, microVMs, egress allowlists), so teams can use them without handing over their credentials.
s1_body: Azure first, also GCP, AWS and Hetzner. Terraform, private networking, Front Door and WAF, API Management, hosting reviews and cost estimates.
s2_body: Microservices, message flows (SWIFT, service bus, events), identity and token exchange, data models and migrations. Python, Rust, TypeScript.
s3_body: MCP servers, agent tooling and sandboxes — and search or RAG when the problem really is finding information.
e1_body: Existing systems, constraints, security and compliance rules, the people who will run it.
e2_body: Working software on a real environment early, reviewed with you every sprint.
e3_body: Documented, automated, and maintainable by your team after I leave.
approach_1: I like boring, reproducible infrastructure, clear interfaces and code that stays maintainable. I am allergic to the improper use of the word AI, and use language models where they solve a measurable problem.
approach_2: I work alongside your teams, in your tools and processes, and prefer open source wherever it fits.
oss_varda: Rust CLI that routes markdown tasks to AI agents and runs them in sandboxed containers or microVMs.
oss_switchboard: one API for Signal, WhatsApp and Telegram messaging.
oss_gdrive: upload and export Google Drive files using Drive's own converters.
oss_pagecast: a command palette for any web page, shipped as a Firefox/Zen add-on.
oss_tessera: a macOS window manager in Rust, built around real Mission Control Spaces.
oss_raycast: lists the windows on the screen under the cursor, across Spaces.
talk_lockfiles: a history of virtualenvs and lockfiles.
blog_intro: Cloud, integrations, AI tooling and the occasional detour — written down so the next person (often me) doesn't have to rediscover it.
portfolio_intro: Projects, products and open-source work — the details behind the home page.
